Sad🇵🇸💔|| Palestine, officially known as the State of Palestine, is a country in the Middle East located along the eastern Mediterranean. It consists of the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip. Palestine is a land of immense historical, cultural, and religious importance, with a history stretching back thousands of years. Palestine is home to some of the world’s most historically significant cities and sites. Jerusalem is one of the holiest cities in the world and is sacred to Muslims, Christians, and Jews. Bethlehem is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Jesus Christ, while Jericho is among the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities. Modern Palestinian national identity developed over many generations and became especially prominent during the 19th and 20th centuries. The Palestinian Declaration of Independence was proclaimed in 1988, and in 2012 the United Nations granted Palestine non-member observer State status. Today, most UN member states recognize the State of Palestine. Palestinian culture is rich in traditions including Arabic language and literature, tatreez embroidery, dabke dancing, olive cultivation, traditional cuisine, and strong family and community ties. Despite decades of conflict, displacement, and political division, Palestinians maintain a strong connection to their homeland and a distinct national identity. #palestine #israel #map #maps #fyp

Palestine 1945🇵🇸💖 Palestine,[i][g] officially the State of Palestine,[ii] is a country in the Southern Levant region of West Asia. Situated between the Mediterranean Sea and Jordan River, it comprises the territories of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, both of which are under occupation by Israel. Palestine shares the majority of its borders with Israel, while the West Bank borders Jordan to the east and the Gaza Strip borders Egypt to the southwest. The West Bank is divided between 165 Palestinian enclaves under partial civilian rule by the Palestinian Authority, and Area C, under full Israeli control. Palestine's population exceeds five million; its proclaimed capital is Jerusalem, while Ramallah serves as its de facto administrative center. Situated at a continental crossroad, the Palestine region was ruled by various empires and experienced various demographic changes from antiquity to the modern era. The region has religious significance. The ongoing Israeli–Palestinian conflict dates back to the rise of the Zionist movement, supported by the United Kingdom during World War I. The war saw Britain occupying Palestine from the Ottoman Empire, where it set up Mandatory Palestine under the auspices of the League of Nations. Increased Jewish immigration led to intercommunal conflict between Jews and Palestinian Arabs, which escalated into a civil war in 1947 after a proposed partitioning by the United Nations was rejected by the Palestinians and other Arab nations. The 1948 Palestine war saw the forcible displacement of a majority of the Arab population, and consequently the establishment of Israel; these events are referred to by Palestinians as the Nakba ('catastrophe'). In the Six-Day War in 1967, Israel occupied the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, which had been held by Jordan and Egypt respectively. The Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) declared independence in 1988. In 1993, the PLO signed the Oslo Accords with Israel, creating limited PLO governance in the West Bank and Gaza Strip through the Palestinian Authority (PA). Israel withdrew from Gaza in its unilateral disengagement in 2005. In 2007, internal divisions between political factions led to a takeover of Gaza by Hamas. Since then, the West Bank has been governed in part by the Fatah-led PA, while the Gaza Strip has remained under the control of Hamas. #fyp #xyzbca #palestine #🇵🇸 #edit

There is something deeply heartbreaking about a little girl in Gaza who has already learned to carry responsibilities that most adults would struggle with, yet still finds the innocence to smile when someone points a camera at her. For a brief moment, she forgets what she’s carrying. She’s just a little girl, happy to be noticed, perhaps excited to see herself on someone’s phone. The kind of ordinary, beautiful reaction you would expect from any child her age. But then you remember where she is. You remember that while children elsewhere are choosing which toys to play with, she is navigating a world where even the simplest necessities require effort, patience, and strength. I wonder what her life would look like if she had been born into peace. What her mornings would sound like. What games she would play. What little things would make her laugh until her stomach hurt. And I hope that one day, she gets to discover all of it. Because the most beautiful thing about her smile isn’t how much suffering she can endure. It’s the little girl who is still there, waiting for a world that will finally let her enjoy being a child. 🇵🇸❤️ #palestine #gaza #fyp #freepalestine #humanity

Palestine’s olive harvest is a tradition passed down through generations, rooted in thousands of years of history. Our olive trees are more than a source of food and livelihood. They are symbols of our identity, our connection to the land, and our steadfastness. Every harvest brings families and communities together to pick olives, share breakfast, and celebrate traditions our ancestors practiced long before us. On October 8, our team gathered with children from the Refaat Alareer Camp on agricultural land in Nuseirat to continue this cherished Palestinian tradition. Despite three years of genocide, displacement, and destruction, our people continue to preserve what the occupation has tried to erase. Our roots run deep. Our traditions endure. Our land is our identity. Help The Sameer Project stand with Palestinians in Gaza and support our General Fund.
